Standard. The 6th-commandment 'lo tirtsach' (Ex 20:13). The Hebrew kernel is specifically illegal-killing-of-innocent-life (homicide); distinguished from H2026 harag ('kill', killing-in-warfare-or-justice) and H4191 mut ('die-cause-die', physical-death). KJV 'kill' is too broad; ESV/NIV 'murder' captures the technical-distinction. Concordant 'murder' preserves the moral-juridical kernel.

Standard. Hebrew-loanword preserved. The realm-of-the-dead, the abode-of-all-departed (both righteous and wicked). KJV uses 'hell / grave / pit' contextually — 'hell' is theologically misleading because Sheol in OT is not the place-of-punishment-for-the-wicked but the neutral-realm-of-all-departed. Modern translations split 'grave / Sheol / pit'. Concordant 'Sheol' preserves the Hebrew-technical-term and avoids the post-NT-Christian theological-overlay. The toelichting flags this as a tradition-correction.

Standard. Distinguished from H5117 nuach ('rest', the resting/settling-state). Concordant 'cease' captures the discontinuance-action; the etymological-link to shabbath (H7676) — Sabbath as 'cessation-day' — is preserved through this rendering. Gen 2:2-3 'God shavath from all his work' is the foundational-context.
